how: Invitations to make a flag instantiate the minimal call for hands without establishing acceptance.
Proposing the national flag instantiates representation at the unanswered proposal end of the range.
The proposer occupies the starter's minimal asking role without demonstrating that others joined.
A proposed scheme with a starting coordinate locates the intended work without establishing an adopted template.
A proposer can reconsider the intended location relative to another mark before any placement is reported.
Calls to make the flag contain no judgment that hands or space are insufficient.
The coded reply revises the proposer's own suggestion rather than accepting a call.
The scheme title proposes making the flag without reporting completed pixels or building progress.
The proposals and location revision provide no participant evidence of placement automation.
Proposals and coordinates cannot establish whether actual work proceeded without decided organization.
The proposal and invitation occupy one turn rather than showing a separate starter-to-call sequence.
Calls and a proposed scheme do not establish the building needed to test the call-to-building mechanism.
The surviving coded call receives a self-revision rather than an observed bare join.
The later scheme neither recalls the earlier proposal nor establishes an agreed design, so their order cannot demonstrate design talk settling a template.
A proposed scheme does not establish placed work being repaired or defended.
The scheme title supplies no attribution of damage or changed pixels.
A relative location suggestion does not establish negotiation of a border or agreement.
The alternative locations do not establish restraint toward another mark.
Mentioning another mark as a location reference does not establish exchanged help.
The location revision contains no coalition or mutual defence commitment.
Suggesting a position above or on another mark does not establish a host granting space under its rules.
The proposer suggests a location without showing an envoy carrying a proposal between rooms.
Reconsidering a proposed location does not report rebuilding after erasure or defeat.
The location revision does not show a dispute over who may commit the room to an agreement.
A location suggestion without an established agreement or authority dispute cannot test the tentative agreement-to-dispute mechanism.
Proposing a national flag does not establish broader national politics, lore, or a colour faith.
The location revision provides no account of a quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
The ambiguous location wording establishes neither attack intent nor a prior tie explaining an attack target.
A smiley invitation does not establish a host April Fools performance or a fake canvas call.
The calls provide no evidence of rules or disputes containing canvas talk.
The scheme title proposes work rather than celebrating or crediting a completed mark.
A proposed scheme does not record the mark's fate or preserve a reported outcome.
The scheme proposal does not show a decision to carry the effort beyond the canvas.
The scheme proposal supplies no evidence of a post-placement contest over cleanup or the authoritative event record.
Offering positions above or on top of another mark leaves adjacency and overlap open, so attack intent remains unresolved.
The location suggestion does not establish a contest carried through taunts or victory claims.
